text:

path: App Store Reviews/4. Me+ Lifestyle Routine - Daily Planner & Habit Tracker/reviews.jsonl
text:
Very helpful, wish we could add multiple tags Over all, I really like this app. Unlike a lot of habit/routine trackers, it doesn’t lock crucial features like customized repeating days, tagging categories, or the number of tasks you can add behind a paywall. I love that the widgets help to visualize your progress, both in terms of task streaks and with a percentage bar of what you’ve finished that day. 

The ability to add one-off tasks if you want to use this as a to-do list is also nice, even if I don’t personally use it that way. 

I don’t love the premium add popup every time I open the app, but for a free app that’s really not bad at all. 

I do, however, REALLY wish we could give habits/tasks multiple tags. EG. Stretching is both part of my morning routine AND part of my health/fitness journey, so it would be nice to be able to see it under both filters. Honestly if that was an option I would absolutely go up to 5 stars. If there’s somewhere to submit feature requests I would love to know.
interpretation: Wants time and life-area membership together.

path: App Store Reviews/85. Habitica - Gamified Taskmanager - Stay motivated and organized/reviews.jsonl
text:
A party member's #1 pet peeve = vanished!! So, this app I am just beginning to tap into, since I have made it a slow but deep delving into gamifying my life and that of my family (that's Mama and two lil' ones...), it just corrected my most discerning of reviewers, my son Huxley Charles. 

Huxley said he'd accidentally press the (-) when he meant to press the (+) for habits and so he maintained a disdain for the habits. No matter what I said, he refuted my arguments with this seemingly small issue. 

I want to THANK you a million times over, because now our WHOLE family of three can use all main features. 

This app has changed our lives in the most positive ways. I want to thank my daughter Aurora Delphine because she did a cool thing I thought was meaningless at the start: making learning something new about Habitica a DAILY! We can go to her or communicate with Aurora Delphine, and he will tell us or message us something new every day that is a fantastic tip or trick.

We have very very little money right now, but I still bought gems to support because of the major contributions this program has made. We don't even need to make up our own prizes, though I have tried a little bit with that, because we realy think your avatars and mounts and potions are amazing.

Also, thank you for putting the number of "To-Do's" down in red as the Dailies have had. I have been involved in a few (about three) major projects that require an extraordinary amount of To-Do's and this assists in tempering that down a bit when I updated and saw I had "91", most of them due in the next 24 hours. Is it possible? Yes, I have pushed myself way beyond what I thought I could accomplish using these. And it helps I think to add small To-Do's you know you can get done quickly just to lower the number by three by adding five... if that makes sense! The boost I get self-esteem-wise is incredible.

I would like to thank the various Guilds and topics that encourage a person to turn something banal into something that sounds adventerous. I am currenty working on building the creativity of my dailies by doing this with every daily when it becomes possible.

I just now hooked up to the browser functions because I could no longer stand hearing about challenges and not being able to join them. I must say, the social support is there, the lack of structure as far as how many times you hit a (+) or (-) is there, and that gives you the freedom to judge yourself in a special way. It is helpful when I have to hit the (-) because I did a negative habit, but then based on howstrongly I decided and followed through stopping that habit, I will hit that (+) button. 

I have kept up to date on the research surrounding essential habits, habits that tend to have an effect on all other habits. In Habitica, one need not discover which habits are the essential ones, but simply organize life this way in whatever way suits you, and then you find things will indeed begin to go your wayand more positive habits will begin to domino from having some of the habits be these essential "KEY HABITS". 

I like the new icons; I like it showing the date for Dailies more pronounced there, and I can tell right now that my weekly shuffle of Habits, Dailies, and To-Do's will be a lot easier since the icons make me think of them more properly to begin with. 

I will have more to say once I have explored this more. But to our family, we appreciate the reduction in stress and the increase in the beauty of our bodies, our minds, our home, and our relationships. Even in the furthering of our education individually and as a group, and in the need for more social support from the shyest of us to the most outgoing, it has been ongoing for two days shy of two months STRAIGHT for the three of us: a 9.5 year old boy Huxley Charles, a just turned 12 year old girl Aurora Delphine, and a young Mama who has family and creativity proirities galore, that wuld otherwise BURST at the seams but for gamifying this way.

I will also mention that we are right now using Procraster and I am trying out learning IQTell.. we will have to see which email service is the best for filtering my email down to next to nothing (close to Inbox Zero would be GREAT!) and is the most user-friendly. I want to expand my knowledge of coding but that is through the kids who teach me. I hope we can all contribute to Habitica one day! 

And if anyone know sif I shoudl use a certain email client for Inbox Zero that is linked up with all this.. or a calendar that is Moleskine but is saved somewhere other than just on my devices just in case but JUST as beautiful, or anything from IFTTT that makes a great connection or few here that would maybe connect anything like Procraster but NOT Pomodoro.. only because it blocks things that I don't need bocked and it's nothing like the start screen of Procraster... gosh, I LOVE THAT START SCREEN... how are you feeling about your project? Habitica, Open Source some of that how are you feeling and here are some suggestions stuff!!

Okay, we made a HUGE investment - no joke, we are on disability because I have a serious illness and had to give up my promising career as a top surgeon and - well, at east it led me to filmmaking and such.. but 4.99 per month is a good start.

Also, kudos on partnership with "seeds". I am hoping that this company is not limited to certain countries becaiuse women really need micro-loans everywhere. I will check it out. I love the concept though, and will check out play seeds.com.

More later, sorry so long, we are just REALLY GRATEFUL. Also, we are trying to fund my daughter's trip as a Young Leader to Washington, DC, and we are about 1800 away. We have received about 1200 so far though. So I am looking for these online funding sources and scared to ask for money, but for Aurora Delphine, I will do anything. So, hopefully the social good goes in a circle and I can get past my fear of taking donations for her to attend this summit she was nominated for.

path: App Store Reviews/10. Finch - Self-Care Pet - Daily Journal & Habit Tracker/reviews.jsonl
text:
Great app, some very minor issues I’ve been using the app for about a month now and the daily goals feature has been really helpful for me. I’ve had very minimal issues with the app, up until today. 

Previously I was able to write my own goals no problem, but whenever I try to write a goal that is more than 1 word, it deletes all but the first word. When I try to edit it nothing changes, and when I try to delete them from my goals altogether they just keep coming back and, more of them?

There is also some features I would like to see changed/added, for example-
1) If I make a typo in a goal or reflection, the app seems to think it’s an actual word and will register it as one of the purple things/objects(?), and I can’t delete them?
2) I somewhat understand the thought behind it, but it’s frustrating that quite a few of the features are Finch Plus only. Like editing icons for the purple things/objects, or some of the breathing exercises.
3) I’m unsure if this is already a feature and I’ve just not found it, but I would really like to see more colour options for the pet(?), and a setting to be able to edit it later on.
4) It would also be nice to be able to pick from every clothing option when buying, not just what’s in the store that day.
5) Sometimes, if you’ve used/added them enough, personal goals you add will stick and go into the recommended goals for the day, and that is great- I would just find it more useful if I could add personal goals to a section where I can always find and use them, rather than typing them out every day until the app picks up on it.

TLDR; The app is really helpful and I’ve gotten a lot of happiness and motivation out of it in the short amount of time I’ve been using it. I have some small nitpicks, but they’re nothing too important, so I can see past them. If it weren’t for the issues I mentioned I would for sure give 5 stars, this is the only self care app I’ve stuck with for so long and can see myself continuing to use in the future. 😊

interpretation: Category/time editing sluggish; no placement conclusion.

path: Play Store Reviews/2. HabitNow Daily Routine Planner/reviews.jsonl
text: Very intuitive user experience. I wish the tasks had tags. Also, I think the GitHub repo is a bit out of date. Edit: I've been falling down the rabbit hole with this app. One thing that took me a while to figure out how to have a "Backlog" of tasks. Basically a long list that I can review and pick 1 or 2 to do each day. I decided to create an "Ideas" category. Then I excluded "Ideas" from the All filter. Whenever I want to do a task from the backlog I just change the Category to something else
interpretation: Uses category as backlog separate from today; task rather than habit scope.

path: Play Store Reviews/2. HabitNow Daily Routine Planner/reviews.jsonl
text: Great app. Well thought out and looks quite good. Has feature parity with much pricier apps for the most part. I'd like to request a couple of changes: 1. In the "Today" section: upcoming, next 7 days tasks, habits can be displayed. 2. Multiple calendar views. Can be something like weekly, monthly, timeline views 3. Categories should show the entries within that category and not just the edit page for categories. Essentially the filter view but for categories tab.
interpretation: Explicitly wants categories to open member entries, not just category edit page.

path: Play Store Reviews/2. HabitNow Daily Routine Planner/reviews.jsonl
text: Excellent app. Especially I like the add function for measurable habits. I need not calculate every time I make an entry. Suggestion : 1. Can we make this 'add' function permanent once selected. Because'replace' function becomes default for every new entry. I've to select 'add' every time now. 2. Categories option at the bottom menu seems redundant as the option is available already in the top left menu. So the bottom menu space can be used for something else
interpretation: Calls redundant category controls wasteful.

path: Play Store Reviews/3. Loop Habit Tracker/reviews.jsonl
text: I am using it for almost a month and I am very satisfied! So clean, simple and it only have what is needed. I'm just hoping if you could add a graph that shows someone's performance for all the habits - e.i. percentage of daily habits checked vs total habits. also if you could add habits category. let's say, habits for personal development. so far what I'm using for this is the color coding. anyways, thank you for this app. keep it up!
interpretation: Wants aggregate progress plus categories; not total-vs-scheduled filter semantics.

path: Play Store Reviews/3. Loop Habit Tracker/reviews.jsonl
text: Great lightweight simple app that does the job brilliantly!! Would be great if we can categorise habits & add count of days since have was last completed.. Thanks for a great app

path: Play Store Reviews/3. Loop Habit Tracker/reviews.jsonl
text: Great app. I would add a category if possible, and a filter on that (exercise, work related, food etc)
interpretation: Asks for categories and filter.

path: Play Store Reviews/3. Loop Habit Tracker/reviews.jsonl
text: I am loving this app. My feedback is I would love an option to sort the apps how they appear on my screen... For example: sort by time of reminder, sort alphabetically, sort by date added, etc. Maybe also the ability to group a number of habits... For example: habits related to health, food, pets, children, reading, or whatever topic you need or prefer, etc. Hope you can help with this!? Absolutely loving this app though even if you don't make these little changes.
interpretation: General grouping and sorting request.

path: Play Store Reviews/3. Loop Habit Tracker/reviews.jsonl
text: You shouldn't be able to check a habit not scheduled on a particular day. And is there a way to group habits or categorize? Thanks
interpretation: Opposes off-day logging; retain intentional access, do not silently reschedule.
